name: io.github.shashwatgtm/revenue-enablement-mcp
description: Revenue Enablement: 12 deal and sales enablement tools by Helix GTM Consulting

tools.name: account_plan_builder
tools.description: Helps you decide how to grow an account in the next 90 days. You give the account name, plus contacts, products, threats and notes if you have them. You get a strategic account plan: a power map with one row per contact you name, whitespace analysis, competitive questions, an answer for each objection and a 90 day plan. It does not look the account up. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of deal_strategy_coach when you need an account-wide 90-day growth plan spanning contacts and products.

account_name.description: Company/account name. Format is text. For example, "an approved anonymous manufacturer".

industry.description: Industry vertical. Format is text. For example, "manufacturing".

current_arr.description: Current ARR with this account (0 for prospects). Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

known_contacts.description: Known contacts and their roles, one per line or separated by semicolons, for example: Head of RevOps (champion); CFO. Each entry becomes one row, so put other notes in account notes. Format is text.

current_products.description: Products/services they currently use from you. Format is text. For example, "manual invoice review".

expansion_opportunities.description: Potential expansion areas or whitespace. Format is text. For example, "extend the pilot to a second finance team".

competitive_threats.description: Known competitors in the account. Format is text. For example, "renewal decision depends on a documented approval process".

your_solution.description: Your product/service offering. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

account_notes.description: Any additional context about the account. Format is text. For example, "quarterly review completed with the finance lead".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

tools.name: deal_strategy_coach
tools.description: Helps you decide what to do next to move a deal. You give the deal name and stage, plus competitors, stakeholder positions and blockers. You get a deal health score, a strategy for the stage, next steps and risks to handle. Ask the user to confirm blocker status, economic buyer engagement, incumbent status and project status when those facts affect the score; typed facts take precedence over text. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of mutual_action_plan_generator when you need to diagnose deal health and choose the next move.

blocker_status.description: Ask whether any blocker is present. A confirmed typed fact overrides word reading. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "none".

economic_buyer_engagement.description: Ask whether the budget holder actively participates in this decision. Overrides word reading. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "engaged".

incumbent_status.description: Ask whether the buyer already uses a competing supplier. Overrides word reading. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "present".

project_status.description: Ask whether the project is still active. A cancelled project is held, without a close plan. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "active".

deal_name.description: Deal/opportunity name. Format is text. For example, "annual renewal".

deal_value.description: Deal value in the supplied currency, in ordinary units (for example 45000000 for INR 4.5 crore). Format is a JSON number.

currency.description: Optional deal currency. Otherwise read from the deal name or text; if none is supplied, the amount is labelled currency not supplied.

deal_stage.description: Current deal stage. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "prospecting".

days_in_stage.description: Days the deal has been in current stage. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

champion_status.description: Champion identification status. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "no_champion".

economic_buyer.description: Economic buyer name and engagement level. Format is text. For example, "finance director".

competitors.description: Competitors in the deal and their position. Format is text. For example, "the current manual review process".

blockers.description: Known blockers or objections. Format is text. For example, "budget approval pending".

next_steps.description: Currently planned next steps. Format is text. For example, "schedule an exception review with the finance owner".

close_date.description: Target close date. Format is text. For example, "2026-11-17".

your_solution.description: What you are selling. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

tools.name: discovery_question_bank
tools.description: Helps you decide what to ask on a discovery call. You give the framework you use (MEDDPICC, BANT, SPICED, Challenger, Gap Selling or all five) and what you already know about the prospect. You get an opening for the conversation, questions in the language of the prospect's sector and on what your solution covers, questions for each part of the framework, a closing and what to say to an objection. It uses only the inputs you give and says which it did not get. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of customer_interview_kit when you need sales qualification questions for a live opportunity.

contact_permission.description: Optional confirmed fact. Ask whether this person permits further contact; this answer overrides contact-refusal wording in the notes. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "allowed".

framework.description: Discovery framework to use. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "meddpicc".

prospect_industry.description: Prospect industry for context. Format is text. For example, "manufacturing".

prospect_role.description: Role of person you are meeting with. Format is text. For example, "finance director".

known_pain_points.description: Pain points already identified. Format is text. For example, "invoice exceptions delay month-end close".

known_metrics.description: Metrics/KPIs already discussed. Format is text. For example, "median approval time measured monthly".

deal_stage.description: Stage of conversation. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "first_call".

your_solution.description: Your product/solution for relevant questions. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

gaps_to_fill.description: Specific information gaps to address. Format is text. For example, "confirm who approves invoice exceptions".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

tools.name: roi_business_case_builder
tools.description: Helps you decide how to build an ROI case the buyer's finance team can check. You give your solution, its main value driver and the buyer's own figures: an annual value estimate, or current annual cost with the expected improvement percent. With them you get the ROI, payback, three year value and sensitivity. Without them it shows no ROI: it names the inputs to add and gives the structure of the case (the cost lines to price, your quoted results as reference points, the questions to ask). Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of pricing_negotiation_guide when you need a buyer-checkable financial case before negotiating terms. Ask finance for the cash-only annual benefit when an investment decision depends on cash.

customer_name.description: Customer/prospect name. Format is text. For example, "an approved anonymous manufacturer".

industry.description: The customer's industry, in any words. Used for wording and sector notes only: no industry figure is applied to the calculation. A return needs the buyer's own figures (annual value estimate, or current annual cost with expected improvement percent). Format is text. For example, "manufacturing".

company_size.description: Company size tier. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "startup".

annual_revenue.description: Customer annual revenue. Shown as your input; it is not turned into a value. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

employee_count.description: Number of employees. Shown as your input; it is not turned into a value. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

your_solution.description: Your product/solution. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

solution_price.description: Annual cost of your solution. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

primary_value_driver.description: Primary value category. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "revenue_increase".

known_metrics.description: Metrics the prospect shared, or results you can quote. Listed as reference points, never as the buyer's figures; to turn the buyer's figures into the value, give current annual cost and expected improvement percent, or annual value estimate. Format is text. For example, "median approval time measured monthly".

current_annual_cost.description: Optional: what the problem or the current process costs the buyer a year, in dollars (their figure). Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

expected_improvement_percent.description: Optional: the share of that annual cost the buyer expects to save, in percent (their figure). Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

annual_value_estimate.description: Optional: the buyer's own estimate of the annual value in dollars; used as the value when given. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

current_process.description: How they do it today. Separate the ways of working with a semicolon: each becomes a cost line to price. Not used in the calculation. Format is text. For example, "manual invoice review".

implementation_timeline.description: Expected implementation time. Shown in the output; not used in the calculation. Format is text. For example, "six weeks".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

annual_cash_benefit.description: Optional buyer-confirmed annual cash benefit in US dollars, excluding staff time without a cash release. Ask finance to separate cash from non-cash value. Compared with the annual solution price; a cash deficit holds the investment decision. Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

tools.name: mutual_action_plan_generator
tools.description: Helps you decide what has to happen, by whom and when, for a deal to sign on time. You give the deal name and the target close date, plus the current stage, the buyer's champion, economic buyer and evaluators, known requirements and process steps if you have them. You get a close plan both sides can work from, with milestones, owners and dates. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of deal_strategy_coach when you need dated milestones and owners for an agreed close target.

deal_name.description: Deal/opportunity name. Format is text. For example, "annual renewal".

target_close_date.description: Target close date (YYYY-MM-DD). A Saturday or Sunday date moves to the Friday before, and the plan says so. Format is text in YYYY-MM-DD form. For example, "2026-11-17".

current_stage.description: Current deal stage. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "discovery".

buyer_champion.description: Champion name and title. Format is text. For example, "finance director".

economic_buyer.description: Economic buyer name and title. Format is text. For example, "finance director".

technical_evaluators.description: Technical evaluators involved. Format is text. For example, "procurement lead and security reviewer".

procurement_contact.description: Procurement contact if known. Format is text. For example, "procurement lead and security reviewer".

known_requirements.description: Known requirements or evaluation criteria. Format is text. For example, "confirm who approves invoice exceptions".

known_process_steps.description: Known steps in their buying process, separated by semicolons or new lines (for example: Pilot; security review; procurement). Each step becomes its own milestone. Format is text.

blockers.description: Known blockers or concerns. Format is text. For example, "budget approval pending".

your_solution.description: What you are selling. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

tools.name: win_loss_analyzer
tools.description: Helps you decide why you won or lost and what to change. You give the details of one deal, a competitor pattern or a set of deals. You get a short write up that names the outcome, the stated reason in the buyer's words, what the reason points to and what the buyer weighed, then questions for the review call and sector notes. It adds no figure or reason you did not give, and says what a missing outcome or reason would add. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of deal_strategy_coach when you need to learn from completed outcomes and stated buyer reasons.

analysis_type.description: Type of analysis. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "single_deal".

deal_outcome.description: Deal outcome for single deal analysis. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "won".

deal_details.description: Deal details, can be rough notes, CRM export, or structured data. Format is text. For example, "renewal was paused because budget approval was delayed".

loss_reason.description: Stated loss reason (for lost deals). Format is text. For example, "two deals paused after budget review".

competitor_won.description: Competitor who won (if applicable). Format is text. For example, "the current manual review process".

deal_value.description: Deal value. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

sales_cycle_days.description: Length of sales cycle. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

stakeholders_involved.description: Key stakeholders and their positions. Format is text. For example, "procurement lead and security reviewer".

your_solution.description: What you were selling. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

multiple_deals.description: For portfolio analysis: summary of multiple deals. Format is text. For example, "renewal was paused because budget approval was delayed".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

tools.name: proposal_section_writer
tools.description: Helps you decide what to write in one proposal section for a buyer. You give the section you need (such as an executive summary, solution overview or pricing justification), your solution, the buyer's challenges, your differentiators, pricing and success measures. You get that section in sentences built from your inputs, with sector notes. It invents no figure, customer or date, and says once which inputs were not given. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of champion_enablement_kit when you need one seller-authored proposal section for the buyer.

section_type.description: Proposal section to generate. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "executive_summary".

customer_name.description: Customer name. Format is text. For example, "an approved anonymous manufacturer".

customer_industry.description: Customer industry. Format is text. For example, "manufacturing".

primary_audience.description: Adds a one-line note at the top of the executive summary on what this audience looks for. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "c_suite".

customer_challenges.description: Key challenges identified. Format is text. For example, "invoice exceptions delay close".

your_solution.description: Your product/solution. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

key_differentiators.description: Why you vs alternatives. Format is text. For example, "checks invoice exceptions before approval".

pricing.description: Pricing details if relevant. Format is text. For example, "USD 24000 per year".

implementation_approach.description: How you will implement. Format is text. For example, "pilot with one finance team before rollout".

success_metrics.description: Expected outcomes/metrics. Format is text. For example, "median approval time measured monthly".

tone.description: Tone for the proposal (changes only the opening of the executive summary). Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "formal".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

tools.name: email_sequence_generator
tools.description: Helps you decide what to send, and when, to open or restart a conversation. You give the persona, stage and objective (prospecting, nurture, follow up or re engagement), plus your solution, the pain point, value proposition, proof and ask. You get each email with its subject, send day and body, and a note on what you did not give. No placeholder is left in a body, and no result or statistic is invented. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of sales_enablement_content when you need scheduled outreach emails with subjects and send days.

sequence_type.description: Type of email sequence. cold_outreach, warm_follow_up, post_demo and re_engagement have their own templates; the other types return a general outline. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "cold_outreach".

target_persona.description: Target persona (e.g., VP Sales, CTO, CFO). Format is text.

target_industry.description: Target industry for context. Format is text. For example, "manufacturing".

your_solution.description: Your product/solution. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

key_value_prop.description: Primary value proposition. Format is text. For example, "resolve invoice exceptions before month-end".

specific_pain_point.description: Specific pain point to address. Format is text. For example, "invoice exceptions delay month-end close".

social_proof.description: Customer names, stats, or proof points. Format is text. For example, "Company-reported pilot reduced approval time from 12 to 9 days in October 2026.".

call_to_action.description: Desired action (meeting, demo, reply). Format is text. For example, "book a discovery call".

num_emails.description: Accepted but not used yet: each sequence type has a fixed number of emails. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

tone.description: Email tone. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "professional".

sender_context.description: Context about sender (role, shared connections, etc.). Format is text. For example, "account owner following up after discovery".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

tools.name: demo_script_builder
tools.description: Helps you decide what to show in a demo, and in what order. You give the demo type, the persona and the use case, plus the features you must show and the pains you name. You get a timed run from opening to close, with spoken lines and a step for each feature tied to the pains, then discussion, close and follow up lines and sector notes. The answer says where each step came from and what it did not get. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of sales_enablement_content when you need a timed product demonstration tied to the use case.

demo_type.description: Type of demo. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "first_look".

primary_audience.description: Primary demo audience (role/persona). Format is text. For example, "finance leaders at manufacturers".

attendees.description: Other attendees and their roles. Format is text. For example, "procurement lead and security reviewer".

customer_industry.description: Customer industry. Format is text. For example, "manufacturing".

your_solution.description: Your product/solution. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

key_pain_points.description: Pain points to address in demo. Format is text. For example, "invoice exceptions delay month-end close".

competitor_context.description: Competitor being displaced or compared. Format is text. For example, "renewal decision depends on a documented approval process".

demo_duration.description: Demo duration in minutes. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

must_show_features.description: Features that must be demonstrated. Format is text. For example, "exception queue and approval history".

known_objections.description: Known objections to address. Format is text. For example, "The reviewer asked who owns unresolved exceptions.".

desired_outcome.description: What you want to achieve from this demo. Format is text. For example, "resolve invoice exceptions before month-end".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

tools.name: pricing_negotiation_guide
tools.description: Helps you decide how to answer a discount request without giving away margin. You give the negotiation scenario, plus deal value, the discount asked, each side's leverage and who approves. You get a leverage assessment, a value based negotiation strategy, answers to common pushback and a discount approval framework. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of roi_business_case_builder when you need responses and approval guidance for a discount discussion. Ask whether the user has authority to approve the proposed terms.

scenario.description: Negotiation scenario. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "discount_request".

deal_value.description: Current deal value. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

discount_requested.description: Discount percentage requested. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

your_solution.description: Your product/solution. Named in the guide and used, with your leverage, to read the sector and how you charge. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

competitor_price.description: Competitor pricing if known. Format is text. For example, "USD 24000 per year".

value_delivered.description: Quantified value your solution delivers. Used in the value reframe, word for word; the guide adds no value figure of its own. Format is text. For example, "200 to 500 employees".

buyer_leverage.description: Buyer leverage points (size, reference potential, etc.). Format is text. For example, "renewal decision depends on a documented approval process".

your_leverage.description: Your leverage points (unique features, timeline, etc.). Format is text. For example, "renewal decision depends on a documented approval process".

decision_timeline.description: When decision needs to be made. Format is text. For example, "six weeks".

approval_authority.description: Who has final approval on pricing. Format is text. For example, "commercial director approves discounts above 10%".

business_model.description: Optional: how you charge (software subscription, services, connectivity, per transaction, marketplace, hardware plus software, or investment management). Read from your other inputs when left out. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "saas".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

pricing_authority_status.description: Optional confirmed fact. Ask whether the user can approve this price or discount. Free-text role titles do not establish authority; unconfirmed authority holds commitment to terms. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "authorized".

tools.name: champion_enablement_kit
tools.description: Helps you decide what to give your champion to sell internally. You give the asset you need (an executive brief, internal business case, objection responses or presentation talking points), your solution, the customer's situation and the objections you expect. You get the asset in the champion's voice with the recommendation, answers to likely questions, the decision requested, a note on the reader and sector notes. It invents no figure or quote. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of proposal_section_writer when you need an internal asset written in the champion's voice.

asset_type.description: Type of enablement asset. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "executive_brief".

champion_name.description: Champion name. Format is text. For example, "finance director".

champion_role.description: Champion role/title. Format is text. For example, "finance director".

target_stakeholder.description: Who the champion needs to convince. Format is text. For example, "finance director".

your_solution.description: Your product/solution. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

key_value_points.description: Key value points to emphasize. Format is text. For example, "resolve invoice exceptions before month-end".

known_objections.description: Expected objections from stakeholders. Format is text. For example, "The reviewer asked who owns unresolved exceptions.".

competitive_context.description: Competitive alternatives being considered. Format is text. For example, "renewal decision depends on a documented approval process".

budget_context.description: Budget situation and pricing. Format is text. For example, "USD 24000 per year".

urgency_drivers.description: Why act now. Format is text. For example, "an audit review due next quarter".

champion_wins.description: How this makes the champion look good. Format is text. For example, "finance teams chose the documented exception process".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

tools.name: competitive_trap_setter
tools.description: Helps you decide which questions expose the gaps in your main competitor, without negative selling. You give the named competitor, your solution, your strengths and its weak points as you know them. You get the set up, discovery questions, criteria to establish, reference call questions, requirement and scenario traps, commercial terms and tactics for your stage, with sector notes. Every line comes from your inputs and the sector, and none from an invented fact about the competitor. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of competitive_intel when you need discovery questions and evaluation criteria for one competitor.

competitor.description: Primary competitor to position against. Format is text. For example, "the current manual review process".

competitor_weaknesses.description: Known competitor weaknesses. Format is text. For example, "handoffs require manual reconciliation".

your_solution.description: Your product/solution. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

your_strengths.description: Your key differentiators. Format is text. For example, "checks invoice exceptions before approval".

evaluation_stage.description: Stage of competitive evaluation. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "early".

buyer_priorities.description: What the buyer cares most about. Format is text. For example, "renewal decision depends on a documented approval process".

buyer_persona.description: Role of key evaluator. Format is text. For example, "finance director".

trap_type.description: Type of competitive positioning. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "discovery_questions".

business_model.description: Optional: how you charge (software subscription, services, connectivity, per transaction, marketplace, hardware plus software, or investment management). Read from your other inputs when left out. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "saas".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".
